groups.title: System services
groups.description: Background services that ship with the system and keep the clock, the network and local-name lookups working. Each is limited to the one place it needs.

groups.title: App updates
groups.description: Flatpak fetching app updates and app information from Flathub.

groups.title: Tailscale
groups.description: For people who use Tailscale: its sign-in and log servers only. Offered separately because most computers do not run it.

groups.title: Name resolution
groups.description: The system resolver reaching its DNS server. This one allows any address, so it is a separate, deliberate choice with its own confirmation.

entries.why: NetworkManager checks that this network reaches the internet, and spots a sign-in page such as a hotel's, by loading a test page from fedoraproject.org.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower r10: idle and after update, /usr/bin/NetworkManager to fedoraproject.org port 80 over tcp and tcp6. Sender pinned to root, uid 0, as the tower r13 image runs it

entries.why: chronyc asks the local time service (chronyd) how it is doing. It only talks to this computer.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower r10: idle and after update, /usr/bin/chronyc to 127.0.0.1 and ::1 port 323 over udp and udp6. Bound by its path only: it reaches this computer only, and any user may run chronyc

entries.why: chronyd sets the clock by asking Fedora's pool of time servers. Only 2.fedora.pool.ntp.org, the pool name in this image's chrony.conf, is allowed: a time server you add yourself, or one a network hands out, still asks.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower 2026-10-12: owner reports /usr/bin/chronyd floods prompts; the host name is the pool line in /etc/chrony.conf (pool 2.fedora.pool.ntp.org iburst), not a capture of the ask. Sender pinned to the chrony account (uid 994 on the tower r13 image, allocated per build, so looked up)

entries.why: Avahi finds printers, shared folders and .local names on your network by multicast DNS. Only the two fixed multicast addresses are allowed, not any server or computer. Replies Avahi sends straight to one computer still ask.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower 2026-10-12: owner reports /usr/bin/avahi-daemon floods prompts; the destination is the fixed multicast DNS group of RFC 6762, not a capture of the ask. Sender pinned to the avahi account (uid 70, static, on the tower r13 image)

entries.why: Flatpak downloads app updates and app information from Flathub.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower r10: after flatpak update --appstream, /usr/bin/flatpak to dl.flathub.org port 443 over tcp6 (held, so the update timed out). Bound by its path only: the desktop user runs it, and sandboxed apps share that user ID, so a sender pin would add nothing

entries.why: Tailscale signs in and fetches your network's settings and keys from its coordination server. Only that server is allowed. Traffic to other Tailscale computers and relay servers can't be named in one narrow rule, so it still asks.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower 2026-10-12: owner reports /usr/bin/tailscaled floods prompts; the host is Tailscale's documented coordination server, not a capture of the ask. Sender pinned to root, uid 0, as the tower r13 image runs it

entries.why: Tailscale sends its client logs to log.tailscale.com. Only that server is allowed.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower 2026-10-12: owner reports /usr/bin/tailscaled floods prompts; the host is Tailscale's documented log server, not a capture of the ask. Sender pinned to root, uid 0, as the tower r13 image runs it

entries.why: A deny default blocks every lookup until the system resolver may reach its DNS server. That server differs on every network, so this lets it reach any address on port 53. Lookups are not private: whoever runs the server sees them, and any program can send data out inside lookups, since every app's lookups use this rule. Flathub updates, blocklist downloads and NetworkManager's check need it.
entries.evidence: bazzite-tower r10: /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-resolved to the network's DNS server port 53 over udp (left out of v1: owner question S6, decided opt-in). TCP port 53 (truncated and large answers) was not captured. r13 (2026-10-14): it runs as systemd-resolve, uid 990 on that image, not the uid sysusers.d declares, so the uid is looked up
